statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low), Stress 46% (elevated), Confidence 89% (high), dominant mode normal. NQZ26 is coiling in a 29.75-point band, 31,007.25 to 31,037.00, after the 11:30Z bar briefly cleared the 31,061.75 prior close at 31,070.25; the session's four intraday lows are rising.
recommendation: Tail at 7% is the lowest reading of the European session and well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 13:00Z to 15:00Z, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September PMI finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services release, where the published path peaks at 16% and stays inside the low band. Stress at 46% remains elevated and describes a difficult but recoverable environment under a 5.28% 10-year and 90-dollar crude; it does not alter the Tail-derived mapping.
headline: Tail eases to 7% as NQZ26 coils in a 29.75-point band with four rising intraday lows, last 31,017.75 at 12:18:44Z and 0.14% below the prior close after the 11:30Z bar tagged 31,070.25
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 9% on a successful retest of the 30,957.50 session low and an 87-point rally to 31,046.75, while noting that the 31,061.75 prior close had not been reclaimed. It has since been reached. The 11:25Z bar printed 31,070.00 and the 11:30Z bar 31,070.25, both above that close, before the move faded back into the range. Reclaiming and then losing a reference level is two-way behaviour, which is the opposite of the repeated-extension shape that defines Tail.

The current hour is the tightest of the session. Between 12:00Z and 12:18:44Z NQZ26 has held a 29.75-point band, 31,007.25 to 31,037.00, with the last print 31,017.75. That is 44.00 points, or 0.14%, below the prior close and 203.50 points below the 31,221.25 overnight high. The intraday low sequence now reads 30,957.50 at 09:40Z, 30,960.00 at 10:35Z, 30,986.00 at 11:00Z and 31,007.25 at 12:10Z. Four successively higher lows over two and a half hours, each produced by a pullback that was absorbed rather than extended, is direct evidence that mean reversion is functioning. The nine-hour run of lower highs and lower lows that drove Tail to 14% in the 10:00Z hour is fully broken.

Cross-asset alignment is absent, and that is the decisive input. ES at 7,779.25 is up 0.03%, YM at 51,518.00 up 0.08% and RTY at 2,858.70 up 0.27%: Nasdaq is the only negative major index, so there is no index-wide directional impulse for a one-way path to build on. The 10-year sits at 5.28%, one basis point lower on the session, and the 2-year at 4.83% is effectively unchanged, so the aligned-yield amplifier present overnight has gone. WTI at 90.22 is down 0.98%, gold at 4,184.10 is up 0.52% and Bitcoin at 86,058 is up 1.11%, none of which describes a risk-appetite collapse. VIX at 16.12 is up 5.29% but from a 15.31 close and within a 16.07 to 16.38 range, a low-magnitude bid off a low base.

The genuine stress input is European rather than American. The euro touched $1.1161, a 17-month low, France's 10-year reached 4.917% against a 24-year high set last week, and the OAT-Bund spread stands near 146 basis points after the largest weekly widening in 17 years, with Spain's 29 November snap election adding political uncertainty. Transmission to the Nasdaq has nonetheless been modest: the STOXX 600 is up 0.2% at 632.42 even as the CAC 40 falls 0.9% to a six-month low. That combination justifies Stress at 46%, in the elevated band, while leaving Tail at 7%.

Ahead lies the 13:30Z cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September PMI finals and the 14:00Z September ISM Services PMI, the only high-impact US release before Wednesday's 18:00Z FOMC minutes. The published path lifts Tail to 14% and 16% across those two hours as a conditional allowance for a liquidity transition and a scheduled print. Event importance and forecast dispersion inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail until an actual path is observed, so the peak stays inside the low band and all 24 forecast hours map to EA_ON. The invalidation is specific: sustained trade below 30,957.50 on shallow or failed pullbacks, with repeated extension after each failure.

Confidence is 89%. The assessment rests on a verified 5-minute NQ series through 12:18:44Z, current VIX, 10-year and 2-year yields, WTI, gold, Bitcoin, the three other US index futures, European cash indices and the verified seven-day US calendar. The shared Finviz context file was read and rejected as evidence: it carries collectionStatus partial and a generatedAt of 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly six days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 11:00Z contain 23 published Claude assessments and one gap at 06:00Z, which stays explicitly unavailable with null assessment fields. The first ten hours, 12:00Z to 21:00Z on 4 October, held Tail at a flat 3% while Stress ran between 64% and 71%, the signature of a difficult but orderly weekend-adjacent regime. Tail then stepped up through the Globex reopen, reaching 12% at 22:00Z and peaking at 15% in the 01:00Z hour as the overnight high of 31,221.25 was set and left behind. From 02:00Z the path decayed steadily, 13%, 10%, 8%, 8%, to a session low of 6% at 08:00Z, with Stress falling in parallel from 60% to 48%. The European morning then produced the only genuine amplification of the window: 11% and mixed at 09:00Z, then 14% and trend-down at 10:00Z on nine hours of lower highs and lower lows into the 30,957.50 low. The 11:00Z hour published 9% and mixed once that low was retested and held. No published hour in the window left the green band.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour published path runs from 7% now to a peak of 16% in the 14:00Z hour and back to 8% by 11:00Z tomorrow, so every slot maps to EA_ON and green. The elevation is concentrated in the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours and is a conditional allowance for the US cash open, the S&P Global PMI finals and the September ISM Services release, not an assertion that one-way structure has been observed. Stress peaks at 58% alongside it and decays to a 40% overnight trough before rebuilding to 47% into the European morning. Confidence declines monotonically from 89% to 60% with the forecast horizon, marking the point beyond which no price-path evidence exists. Only the current 12:00Z slot states observed structure as fact: the 29.75-point coil, the four rising intraday lows and the brief clearing of the 31,061.75 prior close at 31,070.25. Every later hour is framed as a checkpoint, an assumption or an invalidation. The governing invalidation is unchanged: sustained trade below 30,957.50 with shallow or failed pullbacks and repeated extension would raise Tail quickly, while continued two-way absorption would keep it in single digits.
